scope: Prime-independent bounded-sparsity, bounded-degree homogeneous sums of moving-gap beta continuant/Casoratian monomials against Item265 de-overlapped targets

claims.label: PROVED
claims.claim: Fixed sparsity and degree, coefficient log-height O(log n), and O(n/log n) gap budget per monomial give conservative residual sum height O(n).
claims.evidence: report Section 2 and Item276 one-gap bounds
claims.scope_limit: gaps may move with n but must be specified independently of target factorization

claims.label: PROVED
claims.claim: For homogeneous degree K and every Q|q_n, the scalar-Casoratian sum and primitive residual sum have the same gcd with Q.
claims.evidence: report Section 3; every monomial carries the same boundary unit (-q_(n+1)^2)^K
claims.scope_limit: nonhomogeneous sums have different boundary-unit powers and remain open

claims.label: PROVED
claims.claim: With B the gcd of all residual terms, G0=gcd(Q,B), G=gcd(Q,R), and X=G/G0, the sum-only cancellation quotient X divides R/B.
claims.evidence: report Section 4, exact primewise valuation difference
claims.scope_limit: the residual R is required to be nonzero for a height certificate

claims.label: PROVED_SCOPED_CAPACITY_BOUND
claims.claim: The whole sum-only quotient has log X=O(n)=o(n log n), hence zero Route-1 rate at the Item265 beta saddle.
claims.scope_limit: a locally linear O(n) cancellation factor is not excluded

claims.label: PROVED_ACTUAL_TARGET_IMPLICATION
claims.claim: If Q divides the residual sum, then Q/G0 divides R/B and has logarithmic height O(n).
claims.scope_limit: the common baseline G0 remains an Item282 product-return channel

claims.label: PROVED_SUM_DICHOTOMY
claims.claim: A unique least p-adic term valuation gives v_p(R) equal to that minimum; only tied minima can contribute to the cancellation quotient.
claims.scope_limit: tied cancellation may touch a prime absent from every selected return, but is bounded globally by R/B

claims.label: PROVED_IDENTITY_DICHOTOMY
claims.claim: A nonzero O(n)-height residual cannot force full q_n-divisibility for all large n; an identically zero residual can force homogeneous scalar divisibility but gives no nonzero height bound.
claims.evidence: report Section 7 and log q_n=n log n+O(n)
claims.scope_limit: proper de-overlapped target divisibility is not excluded and obeys the O(n) leftover bound

claims.label: PROVED_PRODUCT_BASELINE_SPLIT
claims.claim: Up to O(log n) coefficient height, the common baseline G0 is captured by any one residual product term and belongs to the Item282 product channel.
claims.scope_limit: Item283 does not bound the unresolved weighted-return baseline

claims.label: PROVED_DEOVERLAP
claims.claim: Every statement holds for any Q dividing q_n/gcd(q_n,D_m), so the clearing reservoir is removed before cancellation capacity is measured.
claims.scope_limit: the transverse matching correlation remains open

claims.label: EXACT_FINITE_ONLY
claims.claim: The deterministic checker replays moving-gap heights, homogeneous scalar reduction, cancellation divisibility, target implication, unique/tied minima, and the zero-identity branch.
claims.scope_limit: cancellation rows are algebraic witnesses only; no prime census or asymptotic extrapolation is performed

claims.label: PROVED_BOOKING_DECISION
claims.claim: The sum-only branch has zero normalized rate, but the open product baseline prevents a new beta capacity reduction; booking remains zero.
claims.scope_limit: Route 1 and every conclusion about e+pi remain open

open: the Item282 product baseline and weighted-return cover
nonhomogeneous sums with different boundary-unit degrees
unbounded sparsity or total degree and arbitrary block or Hankel determinants
the uniform prime-power-height or little-oh squarefull theorem
the clearing-divisor and transverse matching correlation
Route 1 and every conclusion about e+pi
